scope: Fresh installed public baseline wheel versus the final stock-arithmetic Flash1017 candidate wheel through public HTTP chat completions, on one machine, with the model loaded and prefix reuse disabled.
prerequisites: Final candidate must pass the separately frozen 618-task quality/parity gate before any performance run.
Parent reviews this draft, binds candidate wheel/source and quality-result hashes, and freezes harness, plan, fixtures and settings before first output.

Baseline/candidate use the same checkpoint, dependency versions, native assets, Python, hardware and requested startup allocator/cache limits. Actual wired-memory policy remains native to each wheel/profile: the stock server raises its wired limit during startup, while the candidate profile resets it before loading. Record this difference; do not claim identical effective wired limits.
No simultaneous model generation, model grading or other intentional compute-heavy task during timed processes.
memory_limit_interpretation: Requested startup allocator guideline and wired limit: 224 GiB; allocator cache limit: 8 GiB. These are initial calls, not a measurement or guarantee of subsequent effective limits. On the observed machine the stock server raises wired memory to 243.2 GiB; the candidate profile subsequently resets it to 224 GiB. Preserve these declared native profile behaviors, record available startup/load evidence and make no assertion that effective wired limits match.

http.timeout_semantics: per-I/O inactivity, not a cumulative request deadline
http.process_wall_timeout_enforcement: An external supervisor must enforce the declared 5400-second process wall bound; HTTPX does not enforce it and keepalives can prevent read inactivity.

cache_policy.prefix_reuse: disabled through normal settings in both arms; require cached_tokens==0 on every response
cache_policy.engram_rows: Fresh process starts each arm/block. One identical excluded 16K warmup runs first. Retain all natural Engram row-cache state after warmup and through the measured sequence; no private clear or tensor mutation.
cache_policy.row_cache_reporting: Save public/read-only observer snapshots after load, after warmup, before/after each measured request and before shutdown when available. Record cache capacities, row-cache counters and their per-request deltas; missing telemetry is unavailable, never zero.
cache_policy.os_cache: Do not purge. OS file/page caches can persist across processes; counterbalanced process order reduces but does not eliminate this effect.
cache_policy.interpretation: Warm loaded-model performance with known row-cache history, not cold-load or cold-storage performance.

per_process: effective safe settings before and after startup
hardware, requested startup memory limits and observed profile-specific wired-limit evidence
per_request: task_id, block, arm, order and preceding task IDs
client request-start, first-nonempty-content and stream-done monotonic timestamps
all text/reasoning deltas, final finish reason and final usage
server TTFT, prompt_eval_duration, generation_duration and token rates
available row-cache and MTP counters before/after request
Read-only MLX active/cache/cumulative-process-peak bytes outside the HTTP timing interval; peak includes load/warmup and is not per-request or full system resident memory.
observations.ttft: Client TTFT = elapsed from immediately before HTTP request send to receipt of the first SSE event with nonempty choices[].delta.content. Ignore role-only, empty content and usage-only events. Any unexpected reasoning/tool output is recorded and makes first-content interpretation explicit; do not silently count it as prose content.
observations.server_timings: Preserve native usage values without relabeling as client timings. Native rates and durations are rounded by the server. Validate prompt_eval_duration and generation_duration are positive; missing required usage is an invalid measurement, not a zero.
observations.completion_latency: Client stream-done latency includes transport and final usage; report as completed-answer latency only for pairwise identical text and ordinary stop in both arms. Length-stopped requests remain in TTFT and throughput tables but have no completed-answer latency claim.

validity.across_block_text_variation: Report explicitly. Within-arm changes across deterministic repeats trigger investigation; do not silently treat them as timing noise.
validity.failure_policy: Preserve failed or divergent observations, mark the paired qualification incomplete/failed, and do not present a successful overall speed claim. A rerun requires a documented reason and a new immutable run identity.

secondary_metrics: client stream-done latency only on identical nontruncated pairs
analysis.pairing: Compare same workload and block; show all16 pairwise results before any summary. For TTFT/latency use baseline/candidate; for rates use candidate/baseline, so values above1 favor the candidate.
analysis.aggregation: For each metric compute the geometric mean of the two block ratios within each case, then equal-case geometric means separately for synthetic1K (2cases), natural16K (4cases), natural64K (2cases), natural-all (6cases), and optionally all8 (explicitly labeled mixed). Show both block ratios and min/max across cases. Never weight by repetitions as if32 independent workloads existed.
analysis.completion_latency_denominator: Show exact eligible task IDs and completed-pair count. Never combine completed and length-stopped answers, and never call time-to512tokens time-to-complete-answer.
analysis.no_quality_inference: These workloads measure performance. Identical outputs establish paired comparability for these requests, not general model quality. Cite the separate618-task gate for broader bounded quality evidence.
analysis.uncertainty: Two temporal blocks on one device support a reproducible bounded comparison, not population significance, p95/p99 latency, broad confidence intervals or general hardware claims.
analysis.historical_separation: Do not transfer or combine the historical20.06% direct-inference result. This run uses ordinary EOS, greedy sampling, public streaming HTTP and a different final build; it stands on its own.

review_items_before_freeze: Bind final candidate and quality report identities
Bind exact performance client/server observer source
Confirm normal cache override is applied after quality configure and saved before server startup
Freeze all payload/config/harness hashes and ensure no mutable source runtime is used

Reconcile shared_environment with the accepted final quality environments; retain the exact complete package/Python/native/metadata maps in the final plan and enforce the declared process wall bound in the supervisor.
